use_case: Peak forecasting for load management: predicts the day and hour of the G&T monthly coincident peak so the cooperative can send member peak alerts and run water-heater load control
vendor_or_model: AMI vendor peak-forecasting add-on (vendor machine-learning model inside the AMI service)
data_categories: Member-level 15-minute interval usage from about 820 meters; load-control switch status; weather; G&T peak advisories
affects_individuals: Yes (310 enrolled water heaters are switched off for up to 4 hours; all members receive peak alerts). Member interval data is processed by the vendor
human_in_the_loop: General Manager approves every load-control event and member alert after checking the G&T peak advisory; no automatic dispatch
applicable_laws: No AI-specific federal or Florida law identified. Wholesale power contract (demand charge). Load-control program terms. Fla. Stat. 501.171 does not list usage data alone, but POL-04 classifies it Internal. Guidance: NIST AI RMF 1.0
status: Trial since 2026-06-01; continued with conditions 2026-08-31; production decision due 2026-11-30

use_case: AMI vendor analytics that flag meters for possible tampering or energy theft
data_categories: Meter interval data; tamper alarms; account status
consequential_decision_category: None listed in the rubric (flags lead to a field check; any back-billing or disconnection follows the tariff and a human decision)
human_in_the_loop: Meter and Service Technician inspects every flagged meter; the General Manager approves any back-billing; no disconnect is sent from a flag
applicable_laws: Cooperative tariff and service rules (not assessed here)
status: In production; quarterly review of flag accuracy added
